column1: Under the 2017 revised rates, what is the Deputation (Duty) Allowance for a transfer within the same station?
column2: 5% of basic pay, subject to a maximum of Rs. 4500 per month.

column1: Under the 2017 revised rates, what is the Deputation (Duty) Allowance for a transfer involving a change of station?
column2: 10% of basic pay, subject to a maximum of Rs. 9000 per month.

column1: According to the 7th CPC recommendations, at what threshold do the ceilings for Deputation (Duty) Allowance rise by 25%?
column2: Each time the Dearness Allowance increases by 50%.

column1: In the context of deputation pay, what is the defined 'Apex level' limit for basic pay plus Deputation (Duty) Allowance?
For Government servants receiving Non-Practising Allowance (NPA), the total of basic pay, NPA, and Deputation (Duty) Allowance cannot exceed the pay of the _____.
column2: Cabinet Secretary (Rs. 2,37,500).

column1: Term: Basic Pay (in the revised 7th CPC structure)
column2: Definition: The pay drawn in the prescribed Level in the Pay Matrix, excluding personal pay or other types of pay.

column1: Are pay upgradations like MACP or Non-Functional Selection Grade (NFSG) in the parent cadre considered for calculating Deputation (Duty) Allowance?
column2: No, the upgraded basic pay under such schemes is not taken into account.

column1: Under the 2018 amendments, what is the default tenure of deputation if the Recruitment Rules (RRs) for an ex-cadre post do not specify one?
column2: 5 years.

column1: Who is the competent authority to grant a deputation extension for the 6th year?
column2: The Secretary of the borrowing Administrative Ministry (or Chief Secretary in State Government).

column1: An extension of deputation for the 7th year requires the approval of the _____ of the borrowing Ministry/Department.
column2: Minister

column1: According to the 2016 delegation of powers, no extension of deputation beyond _____ years is allowed unless provided in the relevant Recruitment Rules.
What is the mandatory 'cooling off' period after a deputation for posts up to Joint Secretary level?
column2: 3 years.

column1: What is the 'cooling off' requirement for an officer at the Additional Secretary level?
column2: 1 year.

column1: Under the 2024 guidelines, Group 'A' officers are eligible for deputation to State Governments only after completing _____ years of service in their parent cadre.
What is the career-long maximum duration for Group 'A' officers on deputation to State Governments/UT Administrations?
column2: 5 years.

column1: Which committee's approval is required for the deputation of Group 'A' officers of the Central Government to State Governments?
column2: Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC).

column1: The 'cooling off' period is waived if a Central Government officer's next deputation is to a _____.
column2: North-East State.

column1: If an officer overstays their approved deputation period, the period of overstay will not be counted for _____.
column2: Pension

column1: Concept: Technical Resignation
column2: Definition: A resignation treated as a technical formality when a Government servant applies through proper channel for another post and is required to resign the previous post to join.

column1: Term: Lien
column2: Definition: The right of a Government employee to hold a regular post, permanent or temporary, either immediately or upon termination of a period of absence.

column1: For how long can a permanent Government servant typically retain a lien in their parent department after joining another Central/State Government department?
column2: 2 years (extendable to 3 years in exceptional cases).

column1: Under what condition is a Government employee's lien on a post automatically terminated?
column2: When they acquire a lien on a permanent post outside their original cadre.

column1: When a resignation is 'Technical', does the employee lose the benefit of past service?
column2: No, the benefit of past service is preserved for pension and other service-related benefits.

column1: What defines 'same station' for determining Deputation (Duty) Allowance?
column2: The station where the person was on duty before proceeding on deputation, including its urban agglomeration.

column1: Within what timeframe must a borrowing authority obtain a deputationist's option for pay fixation?
column2: Within one month from the date of joining the ex-cadre post.

column1: Under the Central Staffing Scheme (CSS), what is the standard tenure for an officer at the Under Secretary (US) level?
column2: 3 years.

column1: Under the Central Staffing Scheme (CSS), what is the standard tenure for an officer at the Deputy Secretary (DS) level?
column2: 4 years.

column1: Under the Central Staffing Scheme (CSS), what is the standard tenure for an officer at the Director level?
column2: 5 years.

column1: What is the maximum allowable duration for a single spell of 'long-term' international assignment within the first 25 years of service?
column2: 5 years.

column1: How many months of short-term consultancies can an officer undertake during their entire career?
column2: 25 months.

column1: What is the maximum duration for an individual short-term consultancy assignment within a single calendar year?
column2: 3 months (90 days).

column1: How does proforma promotion in the parent cadre affect an officer on deputation who has opted for the ex-cadre pay scale?
column2: The officer may revise their option to draw the parent pay plus deputation allowance if it is more beneficial.

column1: For a vacancy already existing, what is the 'crucial date' for determining age-limit eligibility for deputation?
column2: The last date prescribed for receipt of nominations by the originating Ministry/Department.

column1: In the case of an anticipated vacancy, the crucial date for determining eligibility is the _____.
column2: Date on which the vacancy is expected to arise.

column1: Can Deputation (Duty) Allowance be drawn in addition to a Special Allowance granted in the parent department?
column2: No, parent department special allowance is not allowed in addition to Deputation (Duty) Allowance.

column1: Who bears the expenditure for pension and leave salary contributions during a period of foreign service?
column2: The borrowing organization (or the officer if the organization fails to pay).

column1: What is the advance notice period required for the premature reversion of a deputationist to their parent cadre?
column2: At least three months.

column1: Which body finalizes the selection for GOI foreign posts under the Central Staffing Scheme?
column2: The Civil Services Board (CSB).

column1: Under Rule 15 of the Fundamental Rules, a Government servant's lien can be transferred to another _____ post in the same cadre.
column2: Permanent

column1: Does a Government servant on 'Technical Resignation' need to undergo a fresh medical examination if the standards for the new post are identical?
column2: No, a fresh examination is not required.

column1: How is the pay of a Central Government employee regulated upon deputation to a Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE)?
column2: They are not allowed the option of parent pay plus allowance; their pay is governed by Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) orders.

column1: If an officer receives a proforma promotion to a grade higher than their deputation post, can they extend their tenure?
column2: No extension is allowed beyond the currently sanctioned period in such cases (per 2010 rules, later modified in 2012).

column1: According to the 2012 modification, can an officer seek extension after receiving a proforma promotion to a higher grade pay?
column2: Yes, extensions may be considered as per the general tenure instructions if they opt for the promoted pay.

column1: How is seniority handled for a Government servant who rejoins their substantive post after a Technical Resignation?
column2: Seniority is protected, but the period spent in the other department does not count toward minimum service for promotion.

column1: What is the start date for calculating the 9-year eligibility for deputation for a promotee Group 'A' officer?
column2: The 1st of July of the year of allotment or promotion to the Group 'A' post.

column1: If no extension order is received by the last day of a Group 'A' officer's deputation to a state, what must the officer do?
column2: Relinquish charge and get relieved immediately.

column1: Who acts as the Chairman of the Committee for reviewing extensions of Central Group 'A' officers to State Governments beyond 3 years?
column2: Secretary to Government, Department of Personnel & Training.

column1: Under the 1991 instructions, what is the cooling off requirement for an officer returning from a foreign assignment exceeding 180 days?
column2: Two years.

column1: Officers dealing with an international organization in an official coordinating capacity cannot take up assignments in that organization's Secretariat for _____ years after relinquishing charge.
Are temporary Government servants allowed to retain a lien when moving to outside posts?
column2: No, they must sever connections with the Government and do not retain a lien.

column1: What is the limit for carrying forward Earned Leave (EL) and Half Pay Leave (HPL) upon permanent absorption in a PSU?
column2: An overall limit of 300 days.

column1: How is joining time pay calculated for a Government servant moving to a new post after Technical Resignation?
column2: It is equal to the pay drawn immediately before relinquishing charge in the old post.

column1: For 'Reverse Foreign Service' (PSU to Government), how are leave salary and pension contributions determined?
column2: By mutual consent between the PSU and the Government.

column1: What happens to the balance in a National Pension System (NPS) account when a Government servant submits a Technical Resignation?
column2: The balance and the PRAN (Permanent Retirement Account Number) are carried forward to the new office.

column1: If the pay in a new post after Technical Resignation is lower than the previous substantive pay, is the pay protected?
column2: Yes, pay protection is given in terms of presumptive pay under FR 22-B.

column1: Can a person in a higher grade pay be appointed on deputation to a lower grade pay post within the Central Government?
column2: No, such appointments are generally restricted when pay scales and DA patterns are similar.

column1: Who determines whether a transfer is 'outside the normal field of deployment' for deputation purposes?
column2: The authority which controls the service or post from which the employee is transferred.

column1: Is a temporary appointment made on the personal request of an employee treated as deputation?
column2: No, such appointments are not treated as deputation or foreign service.

column1: For Proforma Promotion under the 'Next Below Rule' (NBR), if the parent cadre level is higher than the ex-cadre post, can that pay be used for Deputation Allowance?
column2: No, the higher basic pay under Proforma Promotion is not taken into account for the allowance.

column1: If an officer moves from a Central Staffing Scheme (CSS) post to a non-CSS post, they are eligible for an additional tenure of _____ years.
What is the tenure for a Chief Vigilance Officer (CVO) on deputation?
column2: Maximum of 5 years.

column1: A Central Government Officer may join the Pension scheme of _____ bodies and the period will not count as qualifying service for Central Government pension.
column2: UN

column1: Are Central Government employees on deputation to State Governments entitled to the leave rules of the borrowing organization?
column2: No, they are generally regulated by the leave rules of the parent organization.

column1: Under the 2017 rules, can an officer draw Deputation (Duty) Allowance during an extension in the 5th year?
column2: Yes, if they have opted for the allowance, it continues during the 5th year extension.
